newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmir leader wants talks with separatist leaders.
newsitem.headline: Kashmir leader wants talks with separatist leaders.

text.p: Farooq Abdullah, whose National Conference party swept local polls in India's Jammu and Kashmir state, said on Wednesday he would beef up a fight against armed militants but hoped to hold talks with separatist leaders.

"We will continue with the security scenario as far as it's concerned, beef it up to meet the challenges," Abdullah, who was expected to be named chief minister of the Himalayan state, told Reuters in an interview in the Indian capital.
Since the outbreak of a separatist rebellion in 1990, India has deployed tens of thousands of soldiers and paramilitary troops in the region to try to stamp out the insurgency.

But Abdullah, whose party won an overwhelming majority in the assembly elections held last month, said he hoped to hold talks with leaders of the All Parties Hurriyat (Freedom) Conference, grouping some 30 separatist organisations.

"I hope they (Hurriyat leaders) will come round and we will talk to each other," he said. "Finally we all have to live there. And we would like to bring them round to thinking in terms of the constitution of India....I think dialogue will continue at all levels."
Under the constitution, Jammu and Kashmir state is an integral part of India but enjoys special, autonomous status.
